children.name: Euptelea pleiosperma Hook.fil. & Thomson
children.description: A deciduous tree or shrub 2-15 m tall with papery, ovate to suborbicular leaves having irregularly dentate margins. The flowers lack petals and sepals, bearing conspicuous red anthers on filiform filaments in April-May before or with the leaves, and produce stalked samara-like fruits. It grows in valley forests at 900-3600 m across central and southern China, extending to Bhutan and NE India. IUCN: Least Concern.
